\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to

 *

 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *

 * be left unmodified.

 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: The investigation plan for the existing Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed call first distinguishes the preceding branch that returns -ENODEV when allowDisconnected is false and disconnected_ is true. Otherwise, it compares currentState against the inclusive range from low to high and checks whether 0 is returned within that range. Outside the range, it checks the order and location of ASSERT, the error log, and the -EACCES return code. overview.md/creation/2.text: 호출자는 동일한 요청을 카메라에 다시 큐에 넣기 전에 `Request::reuse()`를 호출해 요청 상태와 연결된 컨트롤을 초기화해야 합니다.

overview.md/discovery/1.text: `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재할 수 있습니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하려고 하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

overview.md/responsibility/0.text: `Camera`는 하나의 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스를 제공하는 `libcamera`의 중심 객체입니다. `libcamera`는 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()` 함수로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera`의 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 소멸할 수 없습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/0.text: `CameraManager`는 libcamera의 진입점으로, 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며 애플리케이션에 카메라를 제공합니다. 관리자는 모든 `Camera` 객체를 소유하고 핫플러그와 핫언플러그를 처리해 카메라의 수명을 관리합니다. 애플리케이션은 관리자 인스턴스를 만들고 `start()`를 호출해야 합니다. 관리자는 처음에 정지 상태이며, 시작하면 시스템의 카메라를 열거하여 `list()`와 `get()`으로 접근할 수 있습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/1.text: 한 번에 `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 두 번째 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다. 카메라는 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 공유되며 마지막 참조가 해제될 때까지 유효합니다. 애플리케이션이 보유한 모든 카메라 참조를 해제한 뒤에는 `stop()`으로 관리자를 정지할 수 있습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/2.text: `Camera`는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성하는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처의 주 인터페이스를 제공합니다. libcamera는 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()`로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera` 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/0.text: `Camera::createRequest()`가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 `Request::reuse()`로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/2.text: `Request::addBuffer()`가 성공하면 전달된 유효한 `Fence`의 소유권은 대상 버퍼인 `buffer`로 이동합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/3.text: `Request::addBuffer()`가 실패하면 전달받은 `fence`의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 상태를 변경하지 않은 그대로 둡니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/4.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 이 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/5.text: `Request::ReuseBuffers`는 `addBuffer()`로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용할 때는 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/review/1.text: `Request::reuse` 전후의 `status_`·`controls_`·`metadata_` 값과 `status_`에 대한 RequestPending 대입을 조사 기록 항목으로 제안합니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/2.text: `Request::addBuffer()`가 실패하면 전달받은 `fence`의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 변경하지 않은 상태로 남깁니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/3.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/4.text: `Request::reuse`는 `ReuseBuffers` 플래그가 설정된 경우 기존 `bufferMap_`의 각 버퍼에 `setRequest(this)`로 현재 요청을 연결한 뒤 해당 버퍼를 `pending_`에 추가합니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/7.text: `Request::ReuseBuffers`는 `addBuffer()`로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용할 때는 이 플래그를 사용하지 않도록 권고합니다.

camera-requests.md/request/0.text: `Camera::createRequest()`는 애플리케이션이 버퍼와 매개변수를 채워 캡처를 위해 큐에 넣을 수 있는 빈 요청을 만들고, 새 요청을 가리키는 포인터를 반환하며 오류가 나면 `nullptr`을 반환합니다. 반환된 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자는 요청을 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 `Request::reuse()`로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다.

request-diagnosis.md/configuration-failu.text: `CameraConfiguration::validate()`의 `Adjusted`는 구성이 유효해지도록 조정된 결과이며, 모든 스트림의 파라미터가 변경되거나 스트림 구성이 삭제될 수 있습니다.

catalog/bc46f3612ad5edf8.text: CameraManager는 libcamera의 진입점으로서 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인과 연결하며, 애플리케이션이 시스템의 카메라에 접근할 수 있게 합니다. CameraManager::Private::pipelineFactoryMatch는 팩토리로 PipelineHandler를 반복해서 만들고 장치 열거자와의 매칭을 시도하며, 매칭에 실패하면 반복을 끝냅니다. CameraManager 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재할 수 있습니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하려고 하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

catalog/bc46f3612ad5edf8/en.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera. It enumerates devices, associates them with pipelines, and gives applications access to the cameras in the system. CameraManager::Private::pipelineFactoryMatch repeatedly creates PipelineHandler through a factory and attempts to match each one with the device enumerator, ending the iteration when a match fails. Only one CameraManager instance may exist at a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the existing one results in undefined behavior.

catalog/76be26d9aff6a78f.text: Camera는 하나의 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스를 제공하는 libcamera의 중심 객체입니다. libcamera는 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 std::shared_ptr<>로 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create() 함수로 생성해야 합니다. Camera의 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 소멸할 수 없습니다.

catalog/76be26d9aff6a78f/en.text: Camera is the central object of libcamera. It represents a camera that can produce one or more image streams from a single image source and provides the main interface for device configuration and control and image stream capture. libcamera manages the lifetime of camera instances with std::shared_ptr<>, and instances must be created using the create() function, which returns a shared pointer. The constructor and destructor of Camera are private, so instances cannot be created or destroyed directly.

catalog/d25f1452fa370799.text: 호출자는 카메라가 Configured 또는 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::createRequest()를 호출해야 합니다. Camera::createRequest()가 반환하는 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다. 호출자는 동일한 요청을 카메라에 다시 큐에 넣기 전에 Request::reuse()를 호출해 요청 상태와 연결된 컨트롤을 초기화해야 합니다.

catalog/d25f1452fa370799/en.text: The caller must call Camera::createRequest() only when the camera is in the Configured or Running state. Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, and the caller must delete the request. Before queuing the same request to the camera again, the caller must call Request::reuse() to reset the request state and associated controls.

catalog/8314f9669879aa97.text: CameraManager는 libcamera의 진입점으로, 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며 애플리케이션에 카메라를 제공합니다. 관리자는 모든 Camera 객체를 소유하고 핫플러그와 핫언플러그를 처리해 카메라의 수명을 관리합니다. 애플리케이션은 관리자 인스턴스를 만들고 start()를 호출해야 합니다. 관리자는 처음에 정지 상태이며, 시작하면 시스템의 카메라를 열거하여 list()와 get()으로 접근할 수 있습니다.

catalog/8314f9669879aa97/en.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera. It enumerates devices, associates them with pipeline managers, and provides cameras to applications. The manager owns all Camera objects and manages camera lifetimes by handling hotplug and hot-unplug events. An application must create a manager instance and call start(). The manager is initially stopped; when started, it enumerates the cameras in the system, which can then be accessed through list() and get().

catalog/558dba20a0eb0667.text: 한 번에 CameraManager 인스턴스는 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 두 번째 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다. 카메라는 std::shared_ptr<>로 공유되며 마지막 참조가 해제될 때까지 유효합니다. 애플리케이션이 보유한 모든 카메라 참조를 해제한 뒤에는 stop()으로 관리자를 정지할 수 있습니다.

catalog/558dba20a0eb0667/en.text: Only one CameraManager instance may exist at a time, and creating a second instance before deleting the existing instance results in undefined behavior. Cameras are shared using std::shared_ptr<> and remain valid until the last reference is released. After releasing all camera references held by the application, the manager can be stopped using stop().

catalog/cd9a46404b3f200f.text: Camera는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성하는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처의 주 인터페이스를 제공합니다. libcamera는 std::shared_ptr<>로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create()로 생성해야 합니다. Camera 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다.

catalog/cd9a46404b3f200f/en.text: Camera represents a camera that produces one or more image streams from a single image source and provides the primary interface for device configuration and control and image stream capture. libcamera manages the lifetime of camera instances with std::shared_ptr<>, and instances must be created with create(), which returns a shared pointer. The Camera constructor and destructor are private, so instances cannot be created or destroyed directly.

catalog/bad4d843416ee787.text: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

catalog/bad4d843416ee787/en.text: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, and the caller must delete the request. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked.

catalog/5a694810d6c9a44a.text: Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 전달된 유효한 Fence의 소유권은 대상 버퍼인 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 상태를 변경하지 않은 그대로 둡니다. 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 이 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

catalog/5a694810d6c9a44a/en.text: If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence passed to it moves to the target buffer, buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the fence passed to it and leaves its state unchanged. If the fence associated with the buffer is not signaled, the request fails after a timeout, and the fence remains on the buffer. The application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing this buffer in another request.

catalog/cca4d70c9068b259.text: Request::ReuseBuffers는 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용할 때는 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.

catalog/cca4d70c9068b259/en.text: Request::ReuseBuffers retains and reuses buffers previously added with addBuffer(), but does not reuse fences associated with the buffers. Avoiding this flag when using fences is recommended.

catalog/b71f7795442e2da4.text: queueRequest의 반환값을 기록 항목으로 제안합니다. 성공 시 0, 오류 시 음수 오류 코드를 기록하며, 해당 코드는 -ENODEV, -EACCES, -EXDEV, -EINVAL 또는 -ENOMEM일 수 있습니다. Request::reuse 전후의 status_·controls_·metadata_ 값과 status_에 대한 RequestPending 대입을 조사 기록 항목으로 제안합니다. 선두 요청의 상태 조회식 req->status()의 반환값을 기록 항목으로 제안합니다.

catalog/b71f7795442e2da4/en.text: The return value of queueRequest is proposed as an item to record. Record 0 on success or a negative error code on error; the code may be -ENODEV, -EACCES, -EXDEV, -EINVAL, or -ENOMEM. The values of status_, controls_, and metadata_ before and after Request::reuse, and the assignment of RequestPending to status_, are proposed as items to record during investigation. The return value of req->status(), the expression used to check the status of the first request, is proposed as an item to record.

catalog/aacc3202b8c71287/en.text: Camera::createRequest() creates an empty request that the application can fill with buffers and parameters and queue for capture, and returns a pointer to the new request. It returns nullptr if an error occurs. Ownership of the returned request passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914.text: Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권이 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 변경하지 않은 상태로 남깁니다.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914/en.text: Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called. If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of a valid Fence moves to buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the supplied fence and leaves it unchanged.

catalog/11e9818eedbc0693.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다. Request::reuse는 ReuseBuffers 플래그가 설정된 경우 기존 bufferMap_의 각 버퍼에 setRequest(this)로 현재 요청을 연결한 뒤 해당 버퍼를 pending_에 추가합니다. Request::reuse()는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 없으면 bufferMap_.clear()를 호출해 bufferMap_을 비웁니다.

catalog/11e9818eedbc0693/en.text: If a fence attached to a buffer is not signaled, the request fails after a timeout, and the fence remains attached to the buffer. The application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. If the ReuseBuffers flag is set, Request::reuse associates the current request with each buffer in the existing bufferMap_ using setRequest(this), then adds the buffer to pending_. If flags has no ReuseBuffers, Request::reuse() calls bufferMap_.clear() to clear bufferMap_.

catalog/4857d32bfad063f5.text: Request::reuse는 status_를 RequestPending으로 설정한 다음 controls_와 metadata_를 차례로 비웁니다. Request::ReuseBuffers는 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용할 때는 이 플래그를 사용하지 않도록 권고합니다.

catalog/4857d32bfad063f5/en.text: Request::reuse sets status_ to RequestPending, then clears controls_ and metadata_ in that order. Request::ReuseBuffers retains and reuses buffers previously added with addBuffer(), but does not reuse fences associated with the buffers. Avoiding this flag when using fences is recommended.

catalog/3b9e7d91721a9bb4.text: 기존 Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed 호출의 조사 계획으로, 먼저 allowDisconnected가 거짓이고 disconnected_가 참이면 -ENODEV를 반환하는 선행 분기를 구분합니다. 그 밖에는 currentState가 low 이상 high 이하인지 비교하고 범위 안에서는 0을 반환하는지 살펴보며, 범위 밖에서는 ASSERT, 오류 로그, -EACCES 반환 코드의 순서와 위치를 확인합니다. CameraConfiguration::validate()의 Adjusted는 구성이 유효해지도록 조정된 결과이며, 모든 스트림의 파라미터가 변경되거나 스트림 구성이 삭제될 수 있습니다. CameraConfiguration::Adjusted를 받은 호출자는 구성을 주의 깊게 확인해야 합니다.

catalog/3b9e7d91721a9bb4/en.text: The investigation plan for the existing Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed call first distinguishes the preceding branch that returns -ENODEV when allowDisconnected is false and disconnected_ is true. Otherwise, it compares currentState against the inclusive range from low to high and checks whether 0 is returned within that range. Outside the range, it checks the order and location of ASSERT, the error log, and the -EACCES return code. Adjusted in CameraConfiguration::validate() is the result of adjustments made to make the configuration valid, and the parameters of all streams may be changed or streams may be removed from the configuration. A caller that receives CameraConfiguration::Adjusted must carefully check the configuration.

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.

 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *

 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

 * streams from a single image source. It provides the main interface to

camera-model/responsibility/manager.text:
\class CameraManager
 * \brief Provide access and manage all cameras in the system
 *
 * The camera manager is the entry point to libcamera. It enumerates devices,
 * associates them with pipeline managers, and provides access to the cameras
 * in the system to applications. The manager owns all Camera objects and
 * handles hot-plugging and hot-unplugging to manage the lifetime of cameras.
 *
 * To interact with libcamera, an application starts by creating a camera
 * manager instance. Only a single instance of the camera manager may exist at
 * a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the
 * existing instance results in undefined behaviour.
 *
 * The manager is initially stopped, and shall be started with start(). This
 * will enumerate all the cameras present in the system, which can then be
 * listed with list() and retrieved with get().
 *
 * Cameras are shared through std::shared_ptr<>, ensuring that a camera will
 * stay valid until the last reference is released without requiring any special
 * action from the application. Once the application has released all the
 * references it held to cameras, the camera manager can be stopped with
 * stop().
 */

CameraManager *CameraManager::self_

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use

 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.

 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.

 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().

 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: `Request::addBuffer()`는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

findings.condition: 완료된 요청에 대해 completeRequest를 호출할 때이며 취소에도 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다.

findings.timing: 요청은 제출 순서로 반환되며 핸들러는 함수 반환 후 해당 요청에 접근할 수 없습니다.
findings.scope: 호출 스레드와 요청 반환에 관한 API 계약입니다. 실제 애플리케이션 콜백 실행은 별도 관찰 대상으로 제시됩니다.
findings.reason: 소스가 반환 순서와 접근 금지를 명시하고 한영 비교 문구도 의무를 보존합니다. 실제 콜백 실행이나 그 스레드가 검증되었다고 주장하지 않습니다.

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */

 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

findings.claim_quote: 조사 계획으로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 `completeBuffer`를 호출할 때 버퍼 완료 알림과 요청의 버퍼 추적 결과를 확인합니다. 반환값이 `true`이면 요청의 모든 버퍼가 완료된 것이고, `false`이면 그렇지 않습니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 `completeRequest`를 별도로 호출하는지 확인합니다. 두 함수는 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

sources.source_quote:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.

Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

findings.claim_quote: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않으므로, 필요한 경우 호출자가 이 함수들의 동기화를 책임져야 합니다.

findings.claim_quote: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire, configure, and then start the camera. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release it when it has finished using it. The application can start and stop the camera multiple times while it remains acquired, and can also reconfigure it. Because the Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with one another, the caller must synchronize these functions when necessary.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::match() 구현자는 단일 파이프라인에 필요한 모든 미디어 장치를 찾으면 MediaDevice::acquire()를 호출해 장치를 모두 확보한 뒤 해당 Camera 인스턴스를 하나 이상 생성하고 내부에 저장하며 카메라 매니저에 등록한 후 true를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::match() 구현자는 필요한 미디어 장치를 모두 찾지 못한 경우 아직 장치를 확보하지 않았다면 어떤 미디어 장치도 확보해서는 안 되며, 이미 일부를 확보했다면 확보한 장치를 모두 MediaDevice::release()로 해제하고 false를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::match()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출되며, true를 반환하면 새 PipelineHandler 인스턴스가 생성되고 그 인스턴스의 match()가 호출됩니다.

findings.condition: The obligations distinguish finding all devices needed for one pipeline from failing to find them, including whether devices have already been acquired.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler implements match(); the camera manager invokes it.
findings.timing: On success, acquisition precedes camera creation; a true return leads to a new handler instance and another match() call. The call runs on the CameraManager thread.
findings.scope: The claim concerns device acquisition, camera creation and registration for a single pipeline instance.
findings.reason: The source supports the stated success and failure obligations, return values, invocation thread and repeated matching. The supplied peer claims concern other operations; the Korean translation source claim is not supplied for comparison.

 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then

 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *

findings.claim_quote: When the PipelineHandler::match() implementer finds all media devices required for a single pipeline, it must call MediaDevice::acquire() to acquire all the devices, then create and store one or more corresponding Camera instances, register them with the camera manager, and return true. If the PipelineHandler::match() implementer cannot find all required media devices and has not yet acquired any devices, it must not acquire any media devices; if it has already acquired some, it must release all acquired devices using MediaDevice::release() and return false. PipelineHandler::match() is called from the CameraManager thread, and if it returns true, a new PipelineHandler instance is created and its match() is called.

\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

findings.claim_quote: generateConfiguration 호출자는 기본 구성을 가져오려는 사용 사례를 roles에 채워야 합니다. generateConfiguration()이 반환하는 구성에는 선택된 스트림과 각 스트림의 기본 파라미터 정보가 포함됩니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 요청된 roles를 충족할 수 있으면 유효한 CameraConfiguration을 반환해야 하고, 그렇지 않으면 null 포인터를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 어떤 스레드에서든 호출될 수 있으므로, 구현은 스레드 안전성을 갖춰야 합니다.

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface

 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its

 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()

 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in

\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: When processing a request containing a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of parameters, the queueRequestDevice implementer must configure the device so that the parameters are applied to the frames captured into the buffers provided in the request. The queueRequestDevice implementer must return 0 on success or a negative error code on failure. PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice() is called on the CameraManager thread.

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

findings.claim_quote: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환된 뒤에는 더 이상 관리하지 않는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest에 전달할 수 있으며, 이 함수는 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

findings.condition: The handler calls completeRequest for a completed request; calls may be made without submission-order constraints.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls completeRequest on the CameraManager thread and must not access the request after the call returns.
findings.timing: Calls may occur out of order; requests are returned to the application in submission order.
findings.scope: The guarantee concerns request return order and the function-call thread. It does not establish the thread on which an application callback executes.
findings.reason: The source supports each obligation and ordering distinction. The peers describe the same return order and separately distinguish buffer completion and observation of callback execution.

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

findings.claim_quote: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 할당한 요청을 Camera::queueRequest()에 전달하기 전에 최소 한 개의 캡처 버퍼로 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 유효하지 않아 큐에 들어가지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest()로 큐에 넣은 요청의 처리가 완료되면 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 애플리케이션에 알립니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::queueRequest()를 호출해야 합니다.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

findings.claim_quote: 파이프라인 핸들러는 버퍼 완료를 알릴 때 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer를 호출해야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 completeRequest를 명시적으로 호출해야 합니다. completeRequest는 queuedRequests_의 선두부터 확인하여 RequestPending이면 반복을 중단합니다. 그렇지 않으면 대기 버퍼가 없음을 확인한 뒤 요청을 제거하고 requestComplete를 호출하여 애플리케이션에 제출 순서대로 반환합니다.

 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().

 * otherwise

findings.claim_quote: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer on the CameraManager thread when reporting buffer completion. Even when the last buffer completes, the request is not completed automatically, so completeRequest must be called explicitly. completeRequest checks requests starting at the front of queuedRequests_ and stops iterating if a request is RequestPending. Otherwise, it verifies that there are no pending buffers, removes the request, and calls requestComplete to return requests to the application in submission order.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, and the caller must delete the request. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked.

	_d()->disconnect();
	disconnected.emit();
}

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

If the return value is true, all buffers in the request have completed; if it is false, they have not. This function notifies the application that the buffer has completed and updates the buffer tracking information inside the request. The request is not completed automatically even when the last buffer completes, so the pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest() to complete the request.

catalog/db69e50714c5c5b8.text: createIPA 내부 람다는 isSignatureValid(m)이 참이면 T::Threaded 객체를 생성하고, 거짓이면 T::Isolated 객체를 생성합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시의 isValid 검사에 실패하면 오류 메시지 Failed to load proxy를 기록하고 nullptr을 반환합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시가 유효성 검사를 통과하면 해당 프록시를 반환합니다.

catalog/db69e50714c5c5b8/en.text: The lambda inside createIPA creates a T::Threaded object if isSignatureValid(m) is true, and a T::Isolated object if it is false. If the created proxy fails the isValid check, createIPA logs the error message Failed to load proxy and returns nullptr. If the created proxy passes validation, createIPA returns that proxy.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환된 뒤에는 더 이상 관리하지 않는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest에 전달할 수 있으며, 이 함수는 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372/en.text: The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest returns, because it no longer manages that request. The pipeline handler may pass completed requests to completeRequest without ordering constraints, and this function returns the requests to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler must call completeRequest on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/cf09f7c08436100c.text: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 할당한 요청을 Camera::queueRequest()에 전달하기 전에 최소 한 개의 캡처 버퍼로 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 유효하지 않아 큐에 들어가지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest()로 큐에 넣은 요청의 처리가 완료되면 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 애플리케이션에 알립니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::queueRequest()를 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/cf09f7c08436100c/en.text: Before passing a request allocated with createRequest() to Camera::queueRequest(), the application must populate it with at least one capture buffer. A request without a buffer is invalid and is rejected without being queued. When processing of a request queued with Camera::queueRequest() is complete, the camera notifies the application through the requestCompleted signal. The caller must call Camera::queueRequest() only when the camera is in the Running state.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633.text: Camera 상태를 바꾸는 함수를 호출하는 호출자는 필요한 경우 함수 간 동기화를 보장해야 합니다. 호출자는 PipelineHandler::completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633/en.text: Callers of functions that change the state of Camera must ensure synchronization between the functions when necessary. The caller must call PipelineHandler::completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6.text: Camera::start는 isAccessAllowed에 허용 상태 값으로 Private::CameraConfigured를 전달합니다. Camera::start의 호출자는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 이 호출을 동기화해야 합니다. 문서화 대상은 카메라 시작 타이밍입니다.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6/en.text: Camera::start passes Private::CameraConfigured to isAccessAllowed as the allowed state value. The caller of Camera::start must synchronize this call with other functions that affect the camera state. The subject to be documented is the timing of camera startup.

catalog/a881a27754dfaea1.text: 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들은 일반적으로 Camera 클래스에서 서로 동기화하지 않습니다. 호출자는 필요한 경우 이 함수들을 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/a881a27754dfaea1/en.text: Functions that affect camera state generally do not synchronize with one another in the Camera class. Callers must synchronize these functions when necessary.

catalog/71d625cc71d6b2fe.text: Camera::createRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. 호출자는 Camera::start와 Camera::stop을 각각 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/71d625cc71d6b2fe/en.text: Camera::createRequest() is a thread-safe function. Camera::queueRequest() is a thread-safe function. The caller must synchronize Camera::start and Camera::stop respectively with other functions that affect the camera state.

catalog/bae5175c944593b3.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer()와 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청이 완료되면 Camera::requestComplete를 호출해 카메라에 알립니다. Camera::requestComplete는 requestCompleted.emit(request)를 호출해 완료된 요청을 애플리케이션에 알리는 신호를 발행합니다.

catalog/bae5175c944593b3/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() and completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. The same rules apply to cancelRequest() as to completeRequest(). When a request completes, the pipeline handler calls Camera::requestComplete to notify the camera. Camera::requestComplete calls requestCompleted.emit(request) to emit a signal notifying the application of the completed request.

catalog/c37fcd839167ec69.text: Camera::queueRequest가 0을 반환하면 요청을 큐에 넣는 데 성공했음을 의미합니다. 요청이 큐에 들어간 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다. waitingRequests_의 선두 요청에서 prepared_가 거짓이면 순회를 중단하므로 뒤 요청도 전달하지 않습니다. queuedRequests_의 크기가 maxQueuedRequestsDevice_와 같으면 요청 전달을 중단합니다.

catalog/c37fcd839167ec69/en.text: If Camera::queueRequest returns 0, the request was successfully queued. After the request is queued, the camera signals its completion via requestCompleted. If prepared_ is false for the first request in waitingRequests_, iteration stops, so subsequent requests are not delivered either. If the size of queuedRequests_ equals maxQueuedRequestsDevice_, request delivery stops.

catalog/71f5a48be32c91d9.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 버퍼 완료를 알릴 때 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer를 호출해야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 completeRequest를 명시적으로 호출해야 합니다. completeRequest는 queuedRequests_의 선두부터 확인하여 RequestPending이면 반복을 중단합니다. 그렇지 않으면 대기 버퍼가 없음을 확인한 뒤 요청을 제거하고 requestComplete를 호출하여 애플리케이션에 제출 순서대로 반환합니다.

catalog/71f5a48be32c91d9/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer on the CameraManager thread when reporting buffer completion. Even when the last buffer completes, the request is not completed automatically, so completeRequest must be called explicitly. completeRequest checks requests starting at the front of queuedRequests_ and stops iterating if a request is RequestPending. Otherwise, it verifies that there are no pending buffers, removes the request, and calls requestComplete to return requests to the application in submission order.

catalog/bad4d843416ee787.text: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

catalog/bad4d843416ee787/en.text: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, and the caller must delete the request. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked.

catalog/0580b13ddd3e2a51.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeRequest()를 호출해야 하며, 이 함수는 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환하고 핸들러는 함수가 반환된 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 조사 계획에서는 실제 애플리케이션 콜백 실행을 별도로 관찰합니다. Camera::disconnect()는 내부 처리 함수인 _d()->disconnect()를 호출합니다. Camera::disconnect()의 emit 호출은 disconnected 신호를 발행합니다.

catalog/0580b13ddd3e2a51/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. This function returns requests to the application in submission order, and the handler must not access a request after the function returns. The investigation plan separately observes the actual execution of the application callback. Camera::disconnect() calls the internal processing function _d()->disconnect(). The call to emit in Camera::disconnect() emits the disconnected signal.

catalog/14622c29d777207f.text: Camera::queueRequest()는 요청의 각 버퍼에 연결된 stream을 activeStreams_에서 찾은 결과가 end()와 같으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청을 캡처 큐에 넣는 데 성공하면 0을 반환합니다. 요청이 큐에 들어간 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다.

catalog/14622c29d777207f/en.text: Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if the result of looking up the stream associated with each buffer in the request in activeStreams_ equals end(). Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues the request for capture. After the request is queued, the camera signals completion with the requestCompleted signal.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914.text: Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권이 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 변경하지 않은 상태로 남깁니다.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914/en.text: Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called. If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of a valid Fence moves to buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the supplied fence and leaves it unchanged.

catalog/ff80b792d7b9b296.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 생성될 때 호출되며, 파이프라인 핸들러가 해당 요청에 필요한 일회성 초기화를 수행할 기회를 제공합니다. PipelineHandler::registerRequest()가 prepared 신호에 연결한 콜백은 doQueueRequests()를 호출합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 내부 waitingRequests_에 요청을 추가한 뒤, 요청의 prepare에 시간 인자 300ms를 전달합니다.

catalog/ff80b792d7b9b296/en.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() is called when a request is created, giving the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform the one-time initialization required for that request. The callback that PipelineHandler::registerRequest() connects to the prepared signal calls doQueueRequests(). PipelineHandler::queueRequest adds the request to the internal waitingRequests_ of the camera referenced by the request, then passes the time argument 300ms to the request's prepare.

catalog/0a44f001a75e1eb3.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환한 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 해당 요청은 더 이상 파이프라인 핸들러가 관리하지 않습니다. completeRequest는 요청이 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환되도록 합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청에 대해 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest를 호출할 수 있습니다.

catalog/0a44f001a75e1eb3/en.text: The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest returns. The pipeline handler no longer manages that request. completeRequest ensures that requests are returned to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler may call completeRequest for completed requests without ordering constraints.

catalog/6d6ccedbcc8325af.text: PipelineHandler::completeRequest()의 while 루프는 큐 맨 앞 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 break를 실행해 루프를 중단합니다. PipelineHandler::completeRequest()는 대기 중인 요청을 파이프라인에 큐잉할 수 있도록 마지막에 doQueueRequests(camera)를 호출합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer와 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()는 먼저 request->_d()->cancel()을 호출한 다음 completeRequest(request)를 호출합니다.

catalog/6d6ccedbcc8325af/en.text: The while loop in PipelineHandler::completeRequest() executes break to break out of the loop if the state of the request at the front of the queue is Request::RequestPending. At the end, PipelineHandler::completeRequest() calls doQueueRequests(camera) so that pending requests can be queued to the pipeline. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer and completeRequest on the CameraManager thread. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest() first calls request->_d()->cancel() and then calls completeRequest(request).

catalog/2f99a34f98acbb1e.text: 조사 계획으로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeBuffer를 호출할 때 버퍼 완료 알림과 요청의 버퍼 추적 결과를 확인합니다. 반환값이 true이면 요청의 모든 버퍼가 완료된 것이고, false이면 그렇지 않습니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeRequest를 별도로 호출하는지 확인합니다. 두 함수는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/2f99a34f98acbb1e/en.text: As part of the investigation plan, when the pipeline handler calls completeBuffer, check the buffer completion notification and the request's buffer tracking result. If the return value is true, all buffers in the request have completed; if it is false, they have not. A request does not complete automatically even when its last buffer completes, so check whether the pipeline handler calls completeRequest separately. Both functions must be called from the CameraManager thread.

overview/boundary/synchronization.text:
Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.
 *
 * \subsection Camera States

overview/boundary/completion.text:
\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

vendor-integration/request/completion-co.text:
\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

camera-model/concurrency/create.text:
\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

camera-model/concurrency/start.text:
\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().
 *
 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the
 * Configured state as defined in \ref camera_operation, and shall be
 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start(const ControlList *controls)

vendor-integration/boundary/repeat.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

vendor-integration/configuration/generat.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

vendor-integration/configuration/configu.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.
 *
 * When configuring the camera the pipeline handler shall associate a Stream
 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

vendor-integration/integration/synchroni.text:
Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

vendor-integration/request/device-result.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

overview/request/queue.text:
\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.
 *
 * When configuring the camera the pipeline handler shall associate a Stream
 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest
